topic: microphone connection fault invalidated part of the 2026-10-26 live results
what_happened: an earlier live test at 5 cm and -8 dB was reported by the listener as clear amplification; those captures showed mic -27.9 and -24.3 dBFS
during the B binding capture the microphone wire turned out to be loose: the ADC read a constant -4.2 dBFS independent of source level and of gain
after reseating the wire the noise floor is -35.1 dBFS with zero full-scale samples
re-running the same 5 cm / -8 dB point with the healthy microphone gives mic -4.0 dBFS with peak 0.0, i.e. INPUT CLIPPING

conclusion.the_earlier_confirmation_is_not_reproduc: with the wire partly connected the microphone was less sensitive, which is why 5 cm produced only -27.9 dBFS; with a healthy connection the same position clips
conclusion.the_listener_did_hear_amplification: that observation stands, but the level numbers from those runs cannot be used as a calibrated operating point
what_is_trustworthy_now: microphone noise floor -35.1 dBFS with no clipping
open-loop coupling -10 to -12 dB measured on six segments with the healthy microphone
loop stability at -8 dB digital gain: loop gain = -8 + (-11) = about -19 dB, far below unity

new_engineering_consequence: the limiting factor at 5 cm is now the INPUT, not the loop. With coupling near -11 dB there is a large stability margin, so positive digital gain is plausible provided the microphone input does not clip.
next_measurement: hold the talker at 20-30 cm so the peak stays below -6 dBFS, then raise the digital gain above -8 dB (0 dB and above) and let the listener judge; the loop margin allows it
process lesson: when a level reading does not change with the excitation, check the wiring before interpreting it acoustically. This cost three invalid captures today.
not_claimed: no calibrated operating point until the microphone is verified and the input peak is measured at the chosen distance

retracted_by_B_2026_10_27.claim: loop gain = -8 + (-11) = -19 dB, far below unity, so positive digital gain is plausible
retracted_by_B_2026_10_27.why_wrong: the -11 dB figure is the in-band ENERGY AVERAGE. Stability is set by the in-band amplitude PEAK of |H|, which B recomputed as +4.40 dB at 321.9 Hz.
retracted_by_B_2026_10_27.consequence: at 0 dB the loop gain is +4.4 dB and it must howl; do not push toward 0 dB. Any gain decision must use the 321.9 Hz peak, never the broadband average.
retracted_by_B_2026_10_27.consistency: the peak-based margins reproduce both of my measured staircases (silent source: -4 stable 0.19, -3 marginal 0.47, -2 oscillating 1.00; live/phone: 0 full-scale, -4 muddy 0.68, -6 near regeneration 0.37-0.70, -8 stable 0.12-0.16)

also_retracted_2026_10_27: the phrase '5 cm / -8 dB confirmed usable operating point' is withdrawn: the low-band spectral tilt shows the historical runs were at roughly 78 cm, not 5 cm (see discriminate-success-vs-clip-2026-10-27.json)
